pedagogical_depth.justification: Strict L4 met. All five lessons carry expanded_walkthrough blocks of 4000+ chars covering title/rationale/setup/teacher_script/expected_student_responses (4 bands)/common_misconceptions (3 each, paired with concrete recovery_moves). Lesson 1 includes the place-value-as-position repair for digit-order confusion; Lesson 2 includes the hundreds-first comparison rule for the ones-first fallacy; Lesson 3 includes the last-digit rule repair for the digit-counting fallacy; Lesson 4 includes the chunk-of-100 strategy upgrade for the chunk-size mismatch; Lesson 5 includes the match-fraction-to-sharers repair for the half-as-default habit. Five distinct worksheet response_types: write, draw_or_write, circle_or_loop, match, self_rate. Mid-unit formative gate (Place-Value Check-In after Lesson 3) AND unit-level reflection sheet (5 prompts) both present.

instructional_balance.justification: Strict L4 met. CRA progression spans the whole week: concrete (real base-ten blocks, snap cubes, estimation jars, paper cookies, pizza cards) → representational (place-value mat drawings, number-line jumps, hundreds chart sort, fraction circles) → abstract (numerical comparison, fraction notation, equation writing, mental skip-counting). Lesson 2 'Compose, Decompose, Compare' is the keystone for B1.1+B1.2; Lesson 4 'Estimation Stake-Out' upgrades the chunk strategy; Lesson 5 'Fair Shares with Thirds and Sixths' is the capstone integrating B1.6+B1.7 in one play scenario.

clarity_communication.justification: Strict L4 met. All five lessons have expanded_walkthrough blocks with substantial teacher_script (≥3000 chars dialogue), 4 expected_student_responses bands (Confused/Mid/Strong/Stretched), and 3 misconceptions paired with concrete recovery_moves. Every lesson has student_learning_goal starting with 'I can'. Teacher scripts use embodied gestures (the place-value mat anchor, the body-on-floor number-line walk, the cube pair-up, the pizza overlay) so the script is enactable, not just readable. Child-voice 'I can' banners on every worksheet header.
